newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - May 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - May 6.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Tuesday:
* The Clinton Administration is set to to change the method of awarding government contracts which may end racial preferences for some minority-owned businesses.
* The political leader of the Islamic Resistance Movement Hamas, Mousa Mohammed Abu Marzook, was deported by the United States and flown to Jordan.
* Zaire's capital Kinshasa awaits the rumored imminent arrival of rebel leader Laurent Kabila in nervous anticipation.

* Large mutual fund companies like Fidelity Investments, American Express Financial Advisors and Invesco, and small investors were taken in by Bre-X Minerals' tale of a massive gold find in Indonesia.
* New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani will call this week for the formation of a city agency to assist and recruit legal immigrants who seek to become citizens.

* Jennifer McVeigh told a Federal jury her brother Timothy McVeigh, accused of the Oklahoma City bombing, wanted to take action against a tyrannical government which deprived Americans of their rights.
* A jury in North Carolina is considering whether a man who killed two young women in a car crash while he was high on painkillers and beer deserves to die.
